transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20260908-3f9b
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood PM), Raj Patel (CTO, Tesserae Guard), Anya López (Head of Infra), Samir Khan (Security Eng), Maya Turner (Network Ops)

Summary:
Tesserae Guard is evaluating Redwood Private for production inference with strict egress and region residency requirements. They run multi-account AWS, want private endpoints or VPC peering (prefer minimal public exposure), require KMS integration and audit logs, and have throughput/latency SLAs for low-latency inference in EU and US regions. Conversation focused on networking topology options, egress IP control, cross-region peering, and next steps to run a bench test and exchange network artifacts.

Topics discussed:
- Private endpoints vs VPC peering vs transit gateway
- NAT/GW constraints and static egress IP needs
- Cross-account and cross-region peering strategies
- KMS/HSM and key custody for inference workloads
- Security/compliance artifacts (SOC2, audit logs, RBAC)
- Bench testing and Terraform samples

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina Park: All right everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lina from Redwood. Quick intros, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, fine?
[00:07] Raj Patel: Yep that's great, thanks Lina. Raj here, CTO. We've got Anya, Samir, Maya on the call too.
[00:13] Anya López: Hi all, hello.
[00:15] Samir Khan: Hey.
[00:16] Marcus Chen: Marcus from Redwood SE, I'll take the deep network questions.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya from security/product, hi.
[00:23] Maya Turner: Maya, networks.
[00:25] Lina Park: Cool. Quick context — Tesserae Guard is looking at private deployment for inference, low egress footprint, and region gating. Correct? Raj: confirm?
[00:34] Raj Patel: Yep that is right. We're two main AWS orgs, prod in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Primary asks are: no public internet for model calls, hold keys in our KMS/HSM, and predictable egress IPs so our downstream partners can whitelist. We also want to avoid any heavy infra changes.
[00:51] Marcus Chen: Okay, great. So we typically offer three patterns: 1) Private Endpoints where you use AWS PrivateLink to our private control plane, 2) VPC peering from your VPC to a Redwood-managed VPC in the same region, or 3) Dedicated private deployment (customer-managed VPC deployed via our package). Each has tradeoffs.
[01:10] Anya López: Can you expand on the peering pattern? Peering across accounts and regions is a little hairy for us.
[01:16] Marcus Chen: Yeah, peering is per-region and per-account. If you peer your prod account in eu-west-1 to our regional VPC, traffic stays private, but you manage routes and there's no transitive peering — so for cross-region you'd do either additional peers or use Transit Gateway. Also, if you need static egress IPs, we can reserve Elastic IPs on a NAT gateway in our infra or recommend using a proxy in your account.
[01:40] Maya Turner: Wait, if the NAT is in your account, how do we restrict egress into third parties? We need fixed IPs that our partners can whitelist.
[01:48] Marcus Chen: Right. Two options: a) we manage NAT with EIPs that we provide and communicate the IPs — this is common for Dedicated customers, or b) use a customer-side egress proxy — so all outbound goes through your NAT in your account and we route via peering. Option b gives you full control.
[02:06] Samir Khan: From security perspective we prefer option b. We cannot hand EIPs to vendors unless we have control. How does the prefix/KV cache behave across peering? Any data plane stays in the peered path?
[02:18] Marcus Chen: The KV cache and model weights live in the serving layer. For Private and Dedicated, the inference dataplane can be configured to route over the peered link so you won't traverse public nets. Some caches may be multi-tenant unless you pick Dedicated or Private managed in your VPC. There's also encryption in transit — mTLS.
[02:34] Raj Patel: Ok, so to summarize we want: private API surface, KMS integration for model keys, and customer-controlled egress. Also latency target is < 200 ms p95 for small prompt sizes.
[02:46] Marcus Chen: That's achievable in-region, for cross-region calls you might see additional RTT. We can pin model shards to region.
[02:54] Anya López: Do you support AWS PrivateLink endpoints? We like endpoint services inside our VPC.
[02:59] Priya Nair: I can add — PrivateLink works mostly for control-plane traffic; for high-throughput inference, peering or dedicated private deployment tends to perform better. But PrivateLink is great if you want minimal routing changes.
[03:12] Raj Patel: How about pilot effort — we want a quick POC to validate latency, peering, and that KMS flow. What's the recommended setup?
[03:19] Marcus Chen: For a POC we'd recommend a 1-region peering setup: you create a peering from your staging account in eu-west-1 to our staging VPC; you'll place an egress proxy in your account if you want control. We'll deploy a small model instance with quantized weights to validate latency. We'll also demonstrate KMS integration via a customer-managed key and show logs to your SIEM. That should be a 1-2 week slice.
[03:44] Maya Turner: For peering we need the CIDR ranges and a sample Terraform snippet. Can you provide that?
[03:49] Marcus Chen: Yep we have sample Terraform and route tables. I'll attach in Slack/email.
[03:52] Lina Park: Lina chiming in — we'll send pricing ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so you can see cost delta. Also we'll include the runbook for onboarding.
[04:02] Samir Khan: Quick question on KMS — can Redwood call into our KMS via cross-account IAM? Or do you require key material to live in Redwood's account?
[04:11] Priya Nair: We support both. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via an IAM role and only use our orchestration to reference the key ARN; key material remains in your account. For hosted flows, we also offer customer-managed keys in some arrangements but that has slightly more setup.
[04:28] Raj Patel: What about audit logs — we need request-level logging for compliance and retention for 1 year.
[04:34] Priya Nair: We export structured logs and can stream to your S3 or Kinesis; retention is configurable. For Private deployments, logs can be kept inside your VPC and pushed to your SIEM. We'll provide an audit schema.
[04:47] Anya López: Region gating: we need inference only in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. We also need to ensure data residency for EU callers stays in the EU. Can you guarantee that?
[04:58] Marcus Chen: Yes — you can pin model versions to a region. Our routing policy can keep EU-routed traffic to eu-west-1. We also support policy-based routing so calls with user locale set to EU are routed accordingly. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated pinned capacity in the region.
[05:13] Maya Turner: A gotcha — some of our downstream partners block VPC peering or require a Transit Gateway. Does Redwood support Transit Gateway peering?
[05:21] Marcus Chen: We can support Transit Gateway attachments for Dedicated or Private deployments. There are some account limits and cross-account attachments — we'll work with your network team. For Hosted PrivateLink, TGW isn't used; it's peering or PrivateLink primarily.
[05:34] Raj Patel: Anything about IP whitelisting for partner APIs that we need to consider?
[05:38] Marcus Chen: If you want Redwood to make outbound calls to partner endpoints on your behalf, and those partners need static IPs, we recommend routing outbound via your NAT so you control the public IPs. If Redwood calls out directly, we can provide EIPs but many customers prefer to keep egress in their account.
[05:56] Samir Khan: Ok makes sense. One more — can we run the inference nodes within our VPC (customer-managed)?
[06:03] Marcus Chen: Yes, that's essentially Private deployment: we deploy our runtime into your VPC (either via an installer / helm or a managed appliance), and you get full control over networking. That has a longer setup time and licensing/ops fee but gives the strongest isolation and egress control.
[06:17] Anya López: Time/effort estimate for Private install?
[06:20] Marcus Chen: Typically 4-6 weeks from kickoff for a basic private deployment including network setup, IAM, KMS, and basic performance tuning. If you stick to a peering POC it's faster — maybe one to two weeks.
[06:31] Raj Patel: Budget question — what should we expect cost-wise relative to hosted?
[06:35] Lina Park: We'll send ballpark numbers but general rule: Hosted is lowest ops overhead, Dedicated offers predictable throughput/cost tradeoffs, and Private has higher base fees but reduces per-token costs at large scale and gives you full control. We'll add numbers in the follow-up.
[06:50] Maya Turner: Are there any known issues with route table limits or overlapping CIDRs we should watch out for?
[06:56] Marcus Chen: Yes, overlapping CIDRs are a hard blocker for peering — you can't have overlapping IP spaces. Route table entry counts can matter with many peers; Transit Gateway helps there. We'll provide a checklist.
[07:08] Raj Patel: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[07:10] Lina Park: Recap: Redwood to send peering/Terraform samples, SOC2/security pack, and pricing. Customer to share CIDRs, region whitelist needs, and nominate folks to run bench tests. We'll aim to schedule the bench test for next week — Raj/Anya, does 2026-09-15 15:00 UTC work?
[07:26] Raj Patel: That works for me.
[07:28] Anya López: Works.
[07:29] Samir Khan: Fine.
[07:30] Lina Park: Awesome. We'll follow up with an email and the invite. Thanks everyone.
[07:34] Raj Patel: Thanks.
